chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abi Najran, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali عليه السلام was sitting when a funeral passed by him. The people stood when the funeral appeared, so al-Husayn عليه السلام said: “A Jewish funeral once passed by while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was sitting in its path, and he disliked that the funeral of a Jew should pass above his head.”
And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad, who said:

Ali ibn Bilal wrote to him that sometimes a deceased person dies among us and the ground is damp, so we line the grave with teak wood or cover it over— is that permissible? He wrote: “That is permissible.”

key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave in which the deceased is buried
key_terms.بِالسَّاجِ: with teak wood used to line the grave
key_terms.جَائِزٌ: permissible according to the written ruling
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: the Messenger of Allah, cited here as the precedent for the reported action

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia hadith to line or cover a grave when the earth is damp, and what is narrated about standing for a passing funeral?
ai.summary: This report contains two passages related to funerary matters. The first recounts Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام explaining the reason connected to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and standing in relation to a passing جنازة, while the second gives a legal ruling permitting the grave to be lined or covered with wood when the ground is damp.
